claims.text: An ultrathin Al2O3 interlayer between elemental Cr and the zirconium-alloy substrate will prevent premature coating failure.
The Al2O3 interlayer will inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The modified coating will retain protection during normal subcritical-water operation and accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer thickness is approximately 20–50 nm.
A uniform and conformal Al2O3 interlayer can be deposited between the Cr coating and the Zr-alloy substrate.
Normal-operation performance is expected at approximately 300°C in subcritical water for approximately 3000 hours.
Accident performance is expected in steam at 1100–1200°C for up to 300 seconds.
The Al2O3 layer will remain continuous and adherent at the Cr/Zr interface.
Al2O3 acts as a physical and chemical diffusion barrier at the Cr/Zr interface.
Al2O3 has low atomic diffusivity and excellent thermodynamic stability under the proposed conditions.
The Al2O3 barrier impedes the interdiffusion of Cr and Zr atoms.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion minimizes the formation of detrimental intermetallic phases and associated coating failures.
The interlayer preserves the oxidative protection supplied by the elemental Cr coating during normal operation.
Relative to Cr-coated Zr alloy without a barrier, the barrier-bearing samples will exhibit significantly less interfacial Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Reduced interdiffusion will produce better coating integrity and preserved protective performance relative to the unmodified baseline.
Elemental Cr-coated Zr alloy without a diffusion barrier is susceptible to premature failure from Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
The intervention is effective up to approximately 1200°C for accident exposures of approximately 300 seconds.
The intervention is effective at approximately 300°C for continuous exposures of approximately 3000 hours.
Exposure beyond the stated limits or severe thermomechanical stress may cause barrier failure.
Thermal-expansion mismatch and thermal cycling may cause Al2O3 delamination or microcracking.

contradictions.description: The intervention places Al2O3 between Cr and Zr, implying a Cr/Al2O3/Zr stack, whereas the experiment describes 'Al2O3/Cr on Zr-alloy,' which conventionally implies Al2O3 above Cr rather than at the Cr/Zr interface. The experimental stack order is therefore inconsistent or at least ambiguous.
